_comment: Every number rendered on the page, and why anyone should believe it.
This exists because of a rule from Emotion-Timeline's own add-stage skill:
'Every published number is reproducible or cross-checked. No exceptions.
A figure in the README that nobody can regenerate is decoration.' Two
figures in that project failed re-derivation once (an AssemblyAI WER that
went 0.61% -> 0.81%, and an NPEC F1 that no repository records at all),
recompute  scripts/check.mjs recomputes it from the vendored data and
fails the build on a mismatch. `check` names the function.
crosscheck not recomputable from raw rows, but it must agree with a
second independently-recorded value. `check` names that too.
attested   recorded in a named source file and not recomputable here.
Rendered as a figure, never described as reproduced.
`text` is asserted VERBATIM in dist/index.html. That is the part that
matters: it catches a number drifting in the PROSE, which is where they
actually rot, not only in a data file.

claims.note: One mean box for every frame overlaps nothing, because the boxes sit on both sides. This is the point of the section.
runs/holdout/run.json records loss only (best_val_loss 1.310), not IoU. Not recomputable from the repository.
Same evidence class as 0.4675. Would become recomputable by re-evaluating the holdout from model_seed42.pt.

claims.note: Unrecomputable by construction: the test labels were never released. Phrasing names the hidden test set.

claims.source: data/emotion-timeline.json scenes[] vs scenes_whisper[] — PRIMARY emotion of each, i.e. the same classifier over two different transcripts
claims.note: METHOD IS LOAD-BEARING, and this number has already moved once. A scene spanning [start, end) covers every integer second t with ceil(start) <= t < end; truncating end instead drops the last second of every scene and gives 62.1% over 2,667. The check pins the convention, not the digits.

denied.why: An NPEC root-instance-segmentation F1 that no repository records anywhere. It is currently live on the GitHub profile README and must not travel here. Emotion-Timeline's add-stage skill names it as a figure that did not survive re-derivation.
DSL-Learning's claimed ~95% static / ~92% dynamic validation accuracy. Nothing committed in that repository backs either number; the models directory is .gitkeep only.
The superseded AssemblyAI word error rate. Re-derivation over a shared time window gave 0.81%; the old figure counted rows instead of seconds.
The CV-Pipeline group's Azure resource naming. Public in that repo, but it reads badly on a job application and adds nothing.
Live deployment FQDNs from the health-check evidence file. Naming a host implies it is up; that evidence is from 2026-06-08.
The specific vessel named in MARBET's technical documentation. The client relationship is fine to state; the itinerary detail is theirs and should not be amplified.
